text:
Clare (Product): quick sync — acme pilot asked for a private onramp with prewarm + HSM key binding. i want a clear railmap for sequencing across product/runtime/infra/security. can folks confirm major deps and blockers?
Sofia (PM): thanks — main asks from acme: predictable latency (SLA), ability to bring their KM, and a canary window for rollout. timeline: they want pilot in ~6 weeks.
Devin (Runtime): from runtime POV: need model shard prewarm hooks, KV cache warm path, and a fallback model if quantized variant misbehaves. prewarm needs infra signals to allocate GPUs ~5m before traffic.
Mike (Infra): noted. infra needs to provision reserved nodes + network peering for private pilot. also we need KMS network egress rules for HSM — that can take 2 weeks for approval in cloud infra.
Rachel (Security): HSM/KMS is the big risk. we need key lifecycle policy, attestation, and an audit plan. also require a security review of the peering config and IAM roles. estimate 10 business days once we get the request packet.
Anita (Eng): engineering effort: runtime integration + product-facing toggle for canaries. i estimate ~3 dev weeks for the runtime hooks + tests. can we compress by parallelizing infra & security reviews?
Jason (SRE): operationally we need observability for the private control plane — request tracing and token-level cost logs. also a rollback path if latency spikes. SRE can own runbook but need clear SLA lines.
Sofia (PM): so rough critical path: security review (10 bd) -> infra peering & HSM enable (10 bd) -> runtime hooks & prewarm (3w) -> staging canary (1w). total is >6 weeks unless some work overlaps.
Clare (Product): overlap plan: start security packet immediately (Sofia + Rachel). infra to start peering prep in parallel with security (Mike). runtime can start proto hooks now but final integration gated on infra/KMS endpoints.
Devin (Runtime): i can spike a prewarm shim and mock KMS calls this week. will post a short design: notes on cache invalidation and prefix caching.
Mike (Infra): i'll open a peering ticket and tag "acme-pilot". timeline: internal approval ~5 bd, cloud infra provisioning ~3 bd after approval. HSM onboarding still depends on security sign-off.
Rachel (Security): i'll kick off the compliance checklist. Sofia, include the exact KMS vendor and expected IP ranges. also add the required retention/audit SLAs for keys.
Anita (Eng): quick question — are we committing to encrypted KV cache at rest for the pilot? that'll affect runtime code.
Clare (Product): yes — encrypted at rest is required per acme legal. assume KMS-backed envelope encryption.
Jason (SRE): for rollback — if latency >150ms p50 we should auto-fallback to hosted model variant for traffic >=5% and then slide to 100% if issues persist. we can implement that via routing policy.
Devin (Runtime): ok routing + fallback looks doable. will add a small health-check endpoint that indicates cache warm status for routing decisions.
Sofia (PM): convo action items: 1) Rachel: start security packet (due 5bd). 2) Mike: open peering/HSM ticket (due 3bd). 3) Anita/Devin: spike prewarm shim + health endpoint (deliverable: design doc by EOW). 4) Jason: draft rollback routing policy (2bd). 5) Clare/Sofia: align with acme on exact pilot acceptance criteria and runbook (2bd).
Clare (Product): i'm adding a short acceptance checklist for the pilot — will paste here once done. goal: reduce ambiguity so security/infra can scope.
deploy-bot: Deployment created: infra/peering-ticket (ACME-PILOT-142) by Mike.
Mike (Infra): created, linking security packet in the ticket.
Rachel (Security): received ticket link. starting initial review today.
Anita (Eng): design doc posted: https://redwood.internal/docs/spikes/acme-prewarm-shim — contains pseudocode and test plan.
Devin (Runtime): noted the doc and added KV cache invalidation scenarios.
Sofia (PM): thanks everyone. small ask: can team call out any non-overlapping blockers that would force serial work (not able to parallelize)?
Rachel (Security): HSM vendor attestation is a serial blocker — we need completed vendor docs before we can approve network creds. that'll be the longest path if vendor takes time.
Mike (Infra): cloud quota increases for reserved nodes might also be serial (account approvals). i'm pinging cloud ops.
Clare (Product): good flags. next sync Friday 10am to confirm packet progress and infra approvals. if either serial blocker stalls, we'll escalate to execs.
Jason (SRE): i'll draft the runbook stub and post by tomorrow.
Clare (Product): final — please react with :thumbsup: once action items acknowledged so i can update the acme kickoff doc.
